requirements.title: Getting started
requirements.intro: A short first-run sequence. Start with the checkup below; it changes nothing.

items.platform: Platform: choose the package by Entware ABI, not just the CPU name. Administrator UID 0 and working NFQUEUE are needed. An exact module profile was tested for RT-AC87U/384.13_10 and is not automatically applied to other firmware. Do not reflash merely to obtain a green status.
items.dns: SmartDNS assigns DoT/DoH to specific sites and pins IP addresses. DNS selects a service address: different CDN addresses can change a strategy’s result. Share the strategy and DNS together when the result depends on DNS. A DNS reply does not guarantee that the site works.
items.transit: Wizard path: dnsmasq stays on 53, our SmartDNS listens on 127.0.0.1:6054, with a marked postconf block for forwarding. Native local names and DHCP are kept. Restore previous DNS before stopping the runtime. Browsers and VPNs may use their own DNS.
items.ark: ARK presence: a loaded module can interfere with NFQWS2 traffic processing. “Not loaded” is favorable for the queue. Presence depends on firmware and settings. An unknown internal flag does not prove it is enabled. Do not disable absent features. If preparation is needed, back up first and reboot ASUS manually after changing settings; restore is available in the same place.
items.traffic: Clients: select the actual WAN and test client IP. DPI running on the router tests its own traffic, not the phone. An outgoing router request normally uses its WAN address, not LAN. VPNs or another NFQWS2 on the path can change results. Preserve a working communication fallback. IPv6 passes separately unless processing is enabled.
items.verify: Result: process → queue binding → packet reception → complete service response. Test new connections. HTTP 200 with a truncated body is insufficient; redirects and expected API 401 responses do not inherently indicate blocking. An HTTPS page does not prove video, voice or QUIC. On the old 87U the official DPI binary needs a separate compatible build; its ordinary DPI installer is not yet validated.
items.updates: Updates: the new NFQWS2 config and lists are placed alongside as *.notactive. Active files are preserved; merge desired changes manually. Only the initial clean installation creates active files from templates.
items.storage: RAM and USB: RT-AC87U was tested with 256 MiB RAM; this is not a proven minimum. Installation and updates need space for dependencies, packages and backup files. /tmp consumes RAM. Preserve existing Entware installations and storage data.

quick.prepare: Check router mode, Merlin and Entware in /opt. USB storage is recommended for older ASUS routers.
quick.install: Install the IPK for your architecture and open http://router-IP:90.
quick.configure: Choose devices and a strategy, or import JSON. Save the settings.
quick.dns: SmartDNS: choose DNS and sites → Check profile → Connect.
quick.verify: Open the required services on a selected device and test new connections.
quick.recover: For help: Share → Preview. To disconnect SmartDNS: Restore previous DNS.
quick.ark: Check whether ARK is loaded. Prepare ASUS only if needed, then reboot it.
quick.start: Start or restart NFQWS2 after changing its strategy. Check that the queue is bound.

progress.title: Setup steps
progress.explanation: Done means the relevant configuration check passed. Partial means settings exist but still need saving, applying or connecting. Not checked means fresh data is unavailable. SmartDNS provides domain-to-DNS rules and fixed replies. Test sites separately on a selected device; a running process and DNS replies do not prove they work.

report.hint: During collection, open the affected service from a device selected for NFQWS2 processing. Two queue samples take 10 seconds.
report.collecting: Collecting a state snapshot. Generate matching traffic now…
report.partial: This is a partial report: some sources are unavailable. The file identifies them and is still useful for troubleshooting.
report.choose_hint: Choose a file to select the folder and JSON filename.
report.browser_hint: Your browser saves the file. To select a folder each time, enable “Ask where to save each file” in its download settings. A plain HTTP page cannot open the native folder picker itself.
report.saved_browser: The file has been handed to your browser for download.
report.help_purpose: If NFQWS2 fails or the panel cannot identify ARK, this report helps locate the failing stage: firmware and Entware, process startup, ARK, WAN and client selection, rules, queue delivery, or strategy resources.
report.help_safety: Collection only reads the current state. It does not change settings, reset counters, restart services, or reboot the router. It also works with NFQWS2 stopped, provided the web panel itself is available.
report.help_privacy: Passwords, keys, IP/MAC addresses, and the contents of your configuration, lists, and logs are excluded. The JSON stays with you and is never uploaded automatically. Share it for troubleshooting, preferably while the failure is present; it cannot recover the cause of an old outage after a reboot. Sending requires your explicit Send click after preview.

dpi.entware_hint: After installing here, you can also run DPI Detector separately: connect to Entware over SSH and run the command below. It opens the original interactive menu. Results from that run do not appear in WebUI; do not run it alongside a check in this panel.
dpi.purpose: DNS, connection and filtering checks. Installation and running are separate actions.
dpi.router_origin: Measurements originate on the router using its current routes. NFQWS2 and VPNs can affect results. This does not test the client NFQUEUE path.
dpi.limits: Native target lists. Time limits are configurable below; process memory is capped at 192 MiB.
dpi.unavailable: Running is currently unavailable. Other panel features remain independent.
dpi.request_failed: The action could not be completed. Refresh the status and retry if needed.
dpi.install_size: The official download is about 4–6 MB; the compatible older ARM file is already in the package. Network tests do not run.
dpi.install_confirm: Install pinned DPI Detector v5.0.0-alpha.21? SHA256 and a real launch are checked; downloads use TLS. Firmware and network settings are preserved.
dpi.run_confirm: Run the selected groups from the router? Checks generate test traffic. Closing the dialog does not stop the job; use Stop.
dpi.heavy5: I consent to Telegram test downloads and uploads as configured.
dpi.heavy6: I consent to TLS connection bursts using the selected domains, fingerprints and attempt counts.
dpi.partial: This result is partial. Finished groups are preserved; remaining checks are not confirmed.
dpi.no_result: No saved DPI results with completed groups are available.
dpi.attach_snapshot: The selected snapshot is attached. A newer job will not replace it in this dialog. The entire additional JSON is shown below.
dpi.attach_local_only: This server currently accepts only the main report. View and save both files, or uncheck this option to send the main report.
dpi.attach_failed: The attachment could not be prepared. Its result or proof may have expired. Uncheck it to send the main report, or collect a new report to prepare another bundle.
dpi.proxy_help: Optional. Proxy credentials are not saved in preferences or sent in the report.
dpi.advanced_help: An empty config and omitted target lists use native defaults. Edit config, targets, burst and limits here. targets: domains, tcp (id/ip/port/sni objects), sni, burst_domains, quic_unsupported; null and [] use native builtin targets; their actual coverage is shown above. Invalid settings are rejected. ASN_CACHE_FILE: null or asn-cache.json in the isolated run directory. Set the proxy in its separate field. Input limit: 128 KiB.
dpi.burst_help: burst: connections (1–100), timeout (s), gap (0–1000 ms), profiles (all or comma-separated codes), tls (1.3+1.2 / 1.3 / 1.2), alpn (h2 / http/1.1), variant, trace (true/false). config contains original config.yml settings.
dpi.local_private: The full local result may include IPs, DNS, network names and custom targets. Email uses a separate cleaned JSON after preview.
dpi.legend: ✓ ok: a reply was received. timeout: the deadline expired; detected: the detector observed filtering indications. These are router observations, not proof of cause. Timing and cutoff size are shown alongside the status.
dpi.legacy_result: Historical result from the previous limited profile. Full native fields were not retained for this run.
dpi.analysis_result: Cleaned file for analysis and sending. All its data is shown below.
dpi.invalid_options: Check the type, format and allowed range of this option
dpi.messages_truncated: The report size limit was reached: some later messages were omitted. Completed test results remain available.

share.title: Share
share.intro: Choose how you want to help the project. You can review the exact files and save a local copy before sending.
share.link_help: Includes a random code for this installation to connect repeat reports. It is not derived from an IP, MAC or serial number. Unchecked means no code is sent. Model and firmware help compare results; a submitted strategy is not yet verified.
share.preview_steps: First click Preview and review the files. Sending requires a preview and a configured channel with format v4 support. Preview again after changing your selection or text.
share.preview_hint: These are the materials sent only after you click Send. Review text and comments: free text may contain personal information you entered.
share.partial: These are the available results. A partial report does not mean other tests failed.
share.strategy_hint: Blocks were found in the saved config. Select blocks and optionally edit the sending copy. The router configuration will not change. Do not include passwords, personal names or exact addresses.
share.operator_required: Required for sharing a strategy. For example, your home internet provider.
share.no_blocks: No nonempty strategy blocks found. You may choose the sanitized full config.
share.location_hint: Approximate, based on the internet exit. A VPN may show a different region. Location is excluded unless you check this box.
share.location_unavailable: Automatic lookup is unavailable. You can enter a region manually.
share.comment: Comment: what works and under which conditions
share.native_hint: Run the original DPI Detector in an Entware terminal using the command below. Choose tests, press S to save, then refresh this list. You can view the original; sharing creates a sanitized JSON without rerunning tests.
share.dpi_help_title: Why do DPI results differ from my phone?
share.dpi_help_scope: DPI Detector checks the router's own connection. The phone and router may pass through NFQWS2 differently, so a working service on the phone does not guarantee the same detector result.
share.dpi_help_clients: For a phone, computer or another LAN device, use its local IPv4 from the router's client list. If DHCP assigns the address, reserve it for the device or check the list after an address change.
share.dpi_help_address: In Only listed devices mode, add the router's WAN address to the IPv4 processing list for a normal detector run: it is the source of the router's outgoing connections. The LAN address used to open the panel is usually unsuitable. This applies to both single-router and multi-router networks.
share.dpi_help_command: Run the command above in an Entware terminal. The address after src is the source IPv4 for this route; add it to the list, with /32 if needed. Check the entry again if the WAN address changes.
share.dpi_help_all: In All devices mode, the router's own IPv4 traffic through the selected WAN is also processed; no separate address entry is needed. In All except listed devices mode, listed addresses are excluded from processing instead.
share.dpi_help_paths: The command checks the IPv4 route to 1.1.1.1. VPNs, IPv6 and policy routing may send other tests along a different path. Entering NFQWS2 does not guarantee that every test will succeed.
share.install_hint: Install the pinned DPI Detector. Older ARM uses a compatible build of the same source included in the package; other platforms download the official file. Tests run separately and network settings are preserved.
share.legacy_active: A previous operation is still active. New runs from this panel are unavailable.
share.import_partial: Some files were not imported or a list limit was reached. Saved copies remain available; remove unneeded results and refresh.
share.no_results: No saved results yet. After pressing S in the original, click Refresh saved results.
share.delete_confirm: Delete this result from the router? This will not change an already prepared submission snapshot.

smartdns.intro: SmartDNS is a separate utility installed and configured by this panel. Assign DNS to specific sites and pin IP addresses: up to 32 DNS servers, 256 domain-to-DNS assignments and 64 fixed replies.
smartdns.scope: Installation adds a separate engine. DNS changes only after validation and clicking Connect.
smartdns.external: SmartDNS is already running outside this wizard, for example from an earlier manual setup. You can prepare and validate a draft. Management must be transferred before connecting it; the current DNS keeps running.
smartdns.installed: SmartDNS engine is installed and verified.
smartdns.next_step: The command above displays the version. DNS use requires a separate configuration and dnsmasq forwarding: test the local port before forwarding queries. See the setup and rollback guide.
smartdns.installing: Installing SmartDNS. You can close this window: the router keeps the result.
smartdns.failed: Installation did not finish. DNS was not switched. Check GitHub access, free space and device compatibility, then retry.
smartdns.request_error: The panel did not reply. Refresh the status: an installation already started continues on the router.
smartdns.unavailable: Installation prerequisites are currently unmet. Supported ARMv7/AArch64 Entware, HTTPS, a correct clock and sufficient resources are required.
smartdns.resources: Download: about 9 MB; engine and libraries: up to 8.1 MiB. The installer checks for 48 MiB free on /opt and 64 MiB available RAM. These are installation reserves, not universal router memory requirements.
smartdns.consent: Install the separate SmartDNS engine from the official release
smartdns.sequence: Add resolvers and sites → validate → review changes → connect and confirm. Validation does not change router DNS.
smartdns.confirm_hint: Check sites from a device on the primary LAN. Confirm if everything works. Without confirmation, previous DNS returns automatically after 120 seconds.
smartdns.validating: Checking settings and SmartDNS startup. Router DNS remains unchanged.
smartdns.switching: Applying or restoring DNS. Reading the current router state…
smartdns.restore_first: Restore previous DNS before replacing a connected profile. Your draft is kept.
smartdns.edited: Edits require a new validation. The previous preview cannot be applied.
smartdns.browser_close: You may close this window: protection runs on the router. Reopening shows its current state. Run the commands below as administrator in the Entware terminal.

form.intro: Default resolvers handle other sites. Assign a resolver to particular sites below. No resolver is preselected: add one you trust.
form.label: Display name
form.default_hint: When selected, this resolver serves sites without a separate DNS rule. Otherwise it serves only sites assigned to it. At least one default resolver is required. Use Connect to enable SmartDNS.
form.default_needed: Select at least one default resolver.
form.domain: Domain without https:// or a path
form.bootstrap_hint: A hostname requires explicit connection IPs. Up to 8 comma-separated addresses of the DNS server, not of the site. Certificate verification stays enabled.
form.records_hint: Pins an IP to a website: the router returns that address instead of asking a DNS server. Useful for a verified service address, such as a poster server. Use an address from a working setup; update or remove the record if it changes.
form.invalid: Check this field and required profile settings.
form.preset_hint: DoT/DoH parameters from the DPI Detector catalog. Selecting a preset fills the fields while preserving sites and the default checkbox. You can enter a custom server. Some DNS providers filter content.
form.short_intro: Set a default DNS; assign others to selected sites.
form.protocol_hint: UDP and TCP are ordinary DNS. DoT uses TLS; DoH uses HTTPS. A preset fills in the parameters. For a custom server, use the settings supplied by its operator.
form.port_hint: The DNS server port: usually 53 for UDP/TCP, 853 for DoT, or 443 for DoH. Enter a different port if the server uses one.
form.address_hint: The address of the DNS server, not a website. If you enter a name, supply its IP (bootstrap) under TLS and connection addresses.
form.sites_hint: These domains will use the DNS server in this card. Including subdomains also covers names such as image.example.org for an example.org rule. Do not enter website IPs here.
form.tls_hint: The name in the DNS server certificate, such as dns.google. It is still required when connecting by IP. DoH also needs the full HTTPS URL supplied by the server operator.

preview.title: DNS preview
preview.scope: Settings and SmartDNS startup were checked. External server replies do not restrict your DNS selection. Test your services after connecting. Local names and DHCP stay with dnsmasq.
preview.overlap: Fixed answers take priority over resolver selection for overlapping domains:
preview.change: Only the primary LAN DNS path changes: dnsmasq on port 53 → our SmartDNS at 127.0.0.1:6054. Native upstream forwarding is temporarily excluded; restoring regenerates it from current native settings. Only our marked block is added to the existing postconf hook. Guest networks, SDN and VPN need separate checks.
preview.checked: Settings checked. You can connect the profile.

errors.native: Working native DNS and an independent recovery path must be verified first. A USB resolver or unknown setting may prevent this. Nothing is disabled automatically; see the checkup and guide.
errors.conflict: Current DNS rules, a hook or unfinished recovery need review. Your draft is kept. The panel preserves the existing DNS settings.
errors.stale: The draft, router DNS or preview validity has changed. Validate again before connecting.
errors.validation: Could not check or connect SmartDNS. Your settings were saved. Check the router state; see diagnostics for details.
errors.busy: Another operation is in progress. Wait for it to finish and refresh the status.
errors.timed_out: The operation timed out. The panel is reading the actual router state; check the DNS restoration message.
errors.restart: dnsmasq did not confirm the switch. Check the DNS state and retry.
errors.memory: Not enough memory to run the check. Retry later or use a smaller profile. Router DNS was not switched.
errors.hook_permissions: Check the DNS script owner and permissions: root ownership and no group or other write access are required (usually 755). The panel did not change DNS.

checkup.title: Router checkup
checkup.readonly: Reads state only. Does not start services, change ARK or test site access.
checkup.write_estimate: write access estimated; no file was written
checkup.hooks: This Merlin integration uses dnsmasq.postconf to forward queries to SmartDNS while retaining DHCP and local names. Starting Entware from USB is a separate task. SmartDNS does not require NFQUEUE or disabling ARK.
checkup.connect_attention: Before connecting, check the current DNS, JFFS, clock, certificates and custom script permission. See the detailed guide. Engine installation and drafts are available separately.
checkup.need_scripts: Enable custom JFFS scripts in Merlin: Administration → System.
checkup.need_jffs: Internal JFFS is needed for independent DNS recovery.
checkup.need_tls: Check the router clock and CA certificate bundle.
checkup.need_review: Review Entware ABI, /opt access and the existing DNS hook in the guide.
checkup.ark_help: This checks whether the ARK module is loaded. It can interfere with NFQWS2 traffic processing: “Not loaded” is a suitable state and gets a check mark. “Unknown” does not mean ARK is enabled. Presence depends on firmware and settings, not just router age. SmartDNS itself does not require disabling ARK.

smartdns.resume_info: Your SmartDNS choice is saved, but the profile is not connected. Load the saved profile, validate and connect it. A new draft does not cancel the previous DNS choice.
smartdns.routing_lost: SmartDNS is running, but dnsmasq no longer forwards queries to it. Check DNS/VPN settings. To reconnect, restore previous DNS, then validate and connect the saved profile.
smartdns.routing_unknown: SmartDNS is running, but DNS forwarding could not be verified. Refresh the status.
smartdns.short_intro: Choose a default DNS or assign a DNS to specific sites.

import.title: Import profile
import.hint: Open your JSON or a cloud preset. All included items are selected; uncheck anything you don't need. JSON is a settings file. Review the changes before saving.
import.allow_shared: I understand that the selected shared settings may affect the other blocks listed in the preview.
import.trust_lua: I trust the source of the selected Lua. NFQWS2 runs them only after a separate service start or restart.
import.allow_incomplete: I understand the listed static analysis limitations. Explicitly missing files and definitions must still be supplied.
import.ready: Changes are ready to save. Review the before / after sections below.
import.needs_choice: Complete the selection using the hints below, then preview again.
import.dns_hint: Select servers with their domains or address records. You edit a copy from the JSON. Only the wizard draft is saved; running DNS is unchanged.
import.save_first: Save or discard unsaved changes in the panel editor first.
import.saved: Selection saved. Restart NFQWS2 separately with its usual button to apply the strategy. DNS is unchanged: check the imported draft in the SmartDNS wizard.
import.undone: Last import undone. Previous config and DNS draft restored; services were unchanged.
import.uncertain: The write reply was not received. Check the result or retry the same write: this will not create a duplicate import.
import.pending: An interrupted write was found. Retrying the same request checks and recovers it.
import.restore_required: Other edits were found after an interruption. Automatic writes stopped to preserve them. The import journal needs checking.
import.error: Unable to read or prepare the data. Check the chosen JSON and retry.

problems.shared_impact: Shared settings also affect the listed blocks. Review the before/after values.

problems.unresolved_blob: The selected block has no unambiguous blob definition. Check shared settings and files.
problems.invalid_dns_profile: Check DNS cards: a default server is required, and DNS hostnames need bootstrap addresses.

problems.empty_selection: Select a block, file, ports or DNS to import.
problems.invalid_file_name: Unsupported file name. Use up to 128 letters A–Z, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores.
